interactions.summary: The seminar reads the Styx crossing, Filippo Argenti's humiliation, the approach to Dis, Dante's fear at the gate, and Virgil's promise that a higher power will open the city.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student reader quoting Inferno with Virgil and Dante dialogue inside the text

interactions.summary: Jiang glosses the scene by saying Virgil has mastered outer hell but is now blocked at the city of Dis, the domain of the fallen angels, where Dante is refused entry.

speaker_notes.note: The ASR mangles 'Dante' as 'donnie,' but Jiang is clearly interpreting Dante's exclusion from Dis.

claims.claim: The quoted canto shows wrath embodied in Filippo Argenti, whose fury degrades him into a mud-soaked object of communal tearing and self-biting.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Inferno material read in the seminar on 2026-06-21.

claims.claim: The city of Dis marks entry into the inner realm of hell ruled by fallen angels, where Virgil's earlier command over the infernal landscape no longer guarantees passage.
Jiang treats Dante's exclusion from Dis as the interpretive point of the scene: hell contains an internal political boundary where even Virgil's status becomes limited.

signature_moments.moment: Virgil's image as the effortless master of hell suddenly breaks at Dis.
signature_moments.source_phrase: virgil is the master of hell ... now we cross the river styx
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This pivot sets up Jiang's larger reading that Virgil's authority is local and fragile rather than absolute.

signature_moments.moment: The blocked gate is answered by the promise that someone else must come unlock the realm.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the one who will unlock this realm for us
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It marks divine intervention as structurally necessary where infernal expertise fails.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The fortified inner city of hell inhabited by fallen angels, where Dante is denied entry and Virgil's authority is tested.
The wrathful Florentine sinner in the Styx whose degradation illustrates anger's infernal condition.

chronology_notes.note: This June 21, 2026 packet introduces Jiang's outer-hell versus inner-hell distinction, which becomes central in the next discussion.

uncertainty_notes.note: The read-aloud translation is noisy in places, but the Styx crossing, Filippo Argenti episode, and transition toward Dis are still clear.
